title: The Heavenly Secrets First Appear
next_chapter_hook: The interrogation results pointed to an unexpected name—an Inner Sect elder of high prestige and virtue.

text.content: The night wind cut like a blade. Before the Servants' Quarters at the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain, Chen Ji stood with hands clasped behind his back, gazing calmly at the more than ten black-cloaked figures surrounding him. The words spoken by that person moments ago still echoed in his ears, yet his face showed not a trace of panic. "Chen family's whelp"—this was a title no one had dared speak in his presence for a long time. Under the moonlight, his gaze was deep as an abyss, and even a faint smile played at the corner of his lips. "Gentlemen, what brings you to visit so late at night?" His voice was unhurried, as if he were not facing a life-or-death situation but simply chatting over tea.

dialogue.content: "My father's debts?" Chen Ji tilted his head slightly, his tone amused. "May I inquire what astronomical sum could possibly warrant such a grand mobilization of distinguished guests?"

text.content: The black-clad leader clearly hadn't expected him to remain so composed; his pupils contracted slightly. The night wind lifted the hem of Chen Ji's thin servant robe. His right hand, hanging at his side, subtly touched his chest—where the Tianji Record Fragment was growing faintly warm. Within three hours, a blood disaster would befall. This was the warning he had risked using the Tianji Record to glimpse this morning, and the assassins before him were the fulfillment of that prophecy. The difference was, he had long since laid preparations in the shadows.

Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, his palm pressing tightly against his chest. In an instant, a golden light—imperceptible to others—flashed from his eyes. The Tianji Record Fragment unfurled dramatically within his consciousness, three silhouettes flickering past like a carousel—First possibility: the enemy would strike first from the left flank with thunderous speed, attempting to take his life within three breaths; Second possibility: the enemy would divide their forces to encircle, advancing methodically to drive him into a dead end; Third possibility... A slight smile curved his lips. The answer was already clear.

He opened his eyes, his gaze calm to the point of being cold. "If you've merely come for a chat, I still have servant duties to attend to." Before the words even finished, his toes tapped the ground, and his form ghosted toward the left. As expected, three assassins on the left flank surged forward first, their short blades gleaming with cold light, aiming directly for his throat—matching the first possibility he had foreseen to the letter.

"Hiss—" A spray of blood. Chen Ji twisted aside to dodge the killing blow, then counter-grabbed a short blade, precisely slicing through the tendon of one assassin's wrist. The man groaned, his blade clattering to the ground. The remaining two pressed their attacks unremittingly, joining forces to夹击, yet Chen Ji blocked with the short blade. Amid the clash of metal, he shifted his footing, stepped on a loose blue stone, and vaulted out of the encirclement using it as leverage. Upon landing, the hem of his servant robe had been sliced off at one corner—exceedingly close.

The black-clad leader's expression shifted slightly, clearly not having anticipated that a Servant Disciple could possess such skill. "All at once! Don't give him a moment to breathe!" More than a dozen figures closed in, their blade and sword light shrouding Chen Ji completely. Yet Chen Ji did not retreat—he advanced instead, his form weaving and darting through the blade light. Every dodge precisely avoided the lethal points; every counterattack precisely struck the enemy's weak spots—wrist, ankle, shoulder blade... all the most vulnerable joints of martial practitioners.

In merely ten breaths, seven men lay groaning on the ground, having lost their combat capability. The remaining few exchanged glances, their hands gripping their weapons trembling slightly. The leader's eyes flashed with a hint of fear, quickly replaced by ruthlessness: "Good! Good one, waste Chen Ji—so you've been hiding your true abilities all along!" He abruptly drew a black talisman from his怀, "Today, either you die or I do—Explode!"

choice.prompt: The talisman's exploding black light engulfed Chen Ji. In this critical moment, he must make a choice:

choices.description: Seize the moment when the enemy is affected by the talisman's blast wave to end the battle at maximum speed, leaving no room for recovery.
choices.visible_reward: Thoroughly crush the enemy,震慑全场

text.content: Chen Ji's form flickered, his afterimage still in place when he had already swept to the enemy leader's front. Before the black light from the exploding talisman had even dispersed, he had slapped his palm against the enemy's chest—this was the ultimate killing move from the third possibility he had foreseen. The black-clad man's pupils contracted sharply; he felt a sharp pain in his chest as his True Qi was instantly sealed, his strength ebbing like a retreating tide. "You... how could—" His voice cut off abruptly because a short blade was already pressed against his throat.

choices.description: First adopt a defensive posture to exhaust the enemy's momentum, observe the overall battlefield situation, then strike—ensuring foolproof execution.
choices.visible_cost: Extended battle duration, consuming more energy
choices.visible_reward: More comprehensively grasp battlefield information, reducing variables
choices.risk_hint: May allow some enemies to escape

text.content: In the instant the black light erupted, Chen Ji had long since utilized the foresight advantage to laterally shift three zhang to the right,稳稳 avoiding the talisman's most fierce blast wave. When the dust settled, he stood with hands clasped behind his back, his robes slightly lifted by the wind, not even a speck of dust on his person. The remaining enemies, having been caught in the talisman's blast to varying degrees, their attacks suddenly faltered. "Gentlemen," his voice carried clearly through the night wind, "who else wishes to repay my father's debts for him?"

The remaining assassins finally realized what kind of terrifying existence this "waste" truly was. Some began retreating, some wore expressions of fear, and others' knees turned soft, directly falling to their knees. The black-clad leader clutched his chest, his face deathly pale, a thin trickle of blood at the corner of his mouth—the previous palm strike had sealed three major acupoints; at this moment, he didn't even have the strength to end his own life.

Chen Ji approached slowly, his gaze sweeping across everyone present, finally settling on the leader. "Speak," his voice was not loud, yet it carried undeniable pressure, "who sent you?" The man clenched his teeth tightly, veins standing out on his forehead, clearly enduring tremendous pain—Chen Ji's acupoint-sealing technique was extremely insidious, amplifying the sensation of pain tenfold. "I... I would rather die than—ah!" Before he could finish, another wave of intense pain struck; he finally couldn't hold on any longer, his scream piercing the night sky.

dialogue.content: "If you won't speak, it makes no difference." Chen Ji squatted down, bringing himself to eye level with the man, a faint smile playing at the corner of his lips. "A few of your men are cowards who value their lives. I only need to ask them." His gaze swept toward the group of trembling assassins. "Gentlemen, who wishes to spare your leader from distress? The first to speak, I will forgive their past offenses."

text.content: The moment these words fell, the effect was immediate. Someone immediately raised their head, a spark of will to survive flickering in their eyes. The leader's expression drastically changed, his voice sharp: "How dare you! If you speak the master's name, do you think any of you will survive—" Before he could finish, a young assassin had already scrambled forward on his knees, embracing Chen Ji's robe hem, his voice shaking: "I-I'll talk! It was... it was an Inner Sect elder who ordered us!"

Chen Ji's eyes slightly hardened. Inner Sect elder—this answer was rather unexpected. Among the Inner Sect, those of high prestige and virtue were numerous; who would go so far as to risk everything, sending assassins to kill a servant disciple like him? His mind raced through calculations, yet his expression remained unchanged. "Which elder? Speak clearly." The man swallowed hard, his voice extremely low: "It was... Elder Zhou. He said... said the Chen family had stolen something that belonged to him, and blood must pay for blood."

choice.prompt: Elder Zhou. Chen Ji quickly retrieved information on this person in his mind. What connection did this person have with his father? Chen Ji faced a choice:

choices.description: Keep this survivor for further interrogation, obtaining more intelligence about Elder Zhou.
choices.visible_cost: Must divert attention to guard the prisoner

text.content: Chen Ji slightly nodded, flicked his hand, and a stream of True Qi sealed the leader's voice point, leaving him only able to watch helplessly as his subordinate revealed all his secrets. "Continue," he looked at the young assassin, "tell me about Elder Zhou and the Chen family's grudge, from the beginning." The man nodded repeatedly, spilling everything he knew like bamboo tubes emptying—in truth, twenty years ago, Elder Zhou had competed with Chen Ji's father for an inheritance, ultimately losing, and had harbored hatred ever since...

choices.description: Kill all survivors, leaving no traces, avoiding information leaks that could bring more trouble.
choices.visible_reward: Avoid information leaks, protect personal safety

text.content: Chen Ji's gaze turned cold. With a flick of his wrist, several sword-qi beams shot forth. Screams rose one after another; a moment later, the back mountain path returned to dead silence. He bent down, retrieving a token from the leader's怀—bearing an ancient, simple character "Zhou." "Elder Zhou," he murmured softly, pocketing the token into his sleeve, "how interesting." Under the moonlight, his smile was chillingly cold. "It seems this waste persona of mine truly offends quite a few people's eyes."

Yet before his voice even faded, Chen Ji's brow center abruptly jumped. An unprecedented dizziness struck him; he stumbled two steps before barely steadying himself by gripping an old tree. The Tianji Record's backlash came faster and more violently than anticipated. He drew a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the surging discomfort, cold sweat already soaking his back. In the previous battle, he had utilized the complete three-hour foresight; although it perfectly predicted every enemy move, it came at a cost—the weakness from the sudden loss of Heavenly Fate was eroding his body in waves.

"Cough..." He coughed softly, raising his hand to wipe away the blood trickling from the corner of his mouth. His Heavenly Fate had decreased by another full ten points. Now his Heavenly Fate was less than thirty percent of his peak; if he forcibly used the Tianji Record again, the consequences would be unimaginable. Worse, this backlash would grow increasingly severe as the Tianji Record Fragment gradually repaired itself—a dangerous vicious cycle. He made a mental note: unless absolutely necessary, never again casually use complete foresight.

Just then, a clear and cold voice drifted from a nearby treetop: "Chen Ji?" Chen Ji's heart tightened. He looked up to see a graceful figure swooping down from the shadows; under the moonlight, that incomparably beautiful face was outlined—the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow Su Qingyao. She stood in white robes atop a branch, gazing down at the chaos below, a complex light flickering in her eyes. "These people are..." Her gaze fell on Chen Ji, her brow slightly furrowing. "You're injured?"

dialogue.content: "Senior Sister Su." Chen Ji forced out a weak smile. "Just a few foolish fools who didn't know their place. Senior Sister needn't worry." As he spoke, he secretly tightened his grip on the token in his sleeve. Su Qingyao was not easy to deceive; if she saw that token, she would definitely interrogate further.

text.content: Su Qingyao leapt down from the branch and approached quickly. She reached out to check Chen Ji's pulse, but he skillfully avoided it without a trace. Her hand hung in mid-air, stiffening for a moment before she nonchalantly withdrew it. "Foolish fools?" She coldly snorted. "Foolish fools at the back mountain Forbidden Grounds, deploying over a dozen assassins with at least Qi Refining seventh stage? Chen Ji, do you take me for a three-year-old?"

Chen Ji sighed inwardly. He had long known Su Qingyao's keen perception; this Inner Disciple Senior Fellow had gotten close to the truth three times, yet he had always cleverly deflected her questions. Tonight's matter would undoubtedly require more explanations. "Since Senior Sister doesn't believe me," he spread his hands in a helpless manner, "then consider me fighting beasts. It's not unusual for sect servants to be attacked by beasts, is it?"

dialogue.content: "You—" Su Qingyao was exasperated. Just as she was about to retort, she saw Chen Ji's form sway, his face pale as paper, almost translucent. She下意识reached out to steady him; the touch was ice-cold. In that instant, her suspicion and anger were suddenly replaced by another emotion—worry. "What exactly is wrong with you?" Her voice unconsciously softened.

text.content: Chen Ji leaned against her arm, weakly smiling: "Thanks for Senior Sister's concern. It's merely an old ailment acting up." He raised his eyes to gaze at the night sky; the starlight was dim, just like his current predicament. Elder Zhou's shadow, the Tianji Record's backlash, Su Qingyao's relentless pursuit... chaos was accelerating its formation, and the pieces in his hand were still far from enough. But tonight, at the very least, he had won another round. "Senior Sister," he said softly, "please keep tonight's matter confidential for me."

Su Qingyao gazed at his pallid features, her heart filled with mixed emotions. This man's secrets ran even deeper and more unfathomable than she had imagined. She should have continued questioning, should have reported this to the sect—yet somehow, facing his vulnerability at this moment, she couldn't bring herself to utter a single word of refusal. "...Fine." She finally sighed. "But you owe me an explanation." Chen Ji slightly nodded, a meaningful arc curving at the corner of his lips: "There will be that day." The night wind brushed past; his lowered eyelashes concealed the scheming within his eyes.
